intent_en: To explain how the weighting of standardized test scores in the U.S. News college ranking formula allows universities to manipulate their rankings.
previous_intent: To illustrate how universities can manipulate U.S. News college rankings by strategically managing standardized test score submissions and average scores to exploit the formula's weighting and discount rules.
narration_support: leaves plenty of room for schools to game the system
chart_support: Pie chart and list of universities (Stanford, Dartmouth, Yale) visualizing the proportion of SAT/ACT scores in the U.S. News ranking formula
evidence_note: The narration explicitly discusses how the formula allows schools to 'game the system' by manipulating submission rates or scores. The chart visualizes the 7.75% weight of SAT/ACT scores and lists top universities, supporting the context of the ranking formula discussion.
